Hurricane Solene Discussion Number 14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL (fictional demo storm)
400 PM CDT Mon Jul 22 2026

Solene remains a well-organized category 2 hurricane this afternoon. A recent microwave pass shows a compact but well-defined eye embedded within deep central convection, with an intact mid-level ring of thunderstorms wrapping most of the circulation. Environmental conditions remain generally favorable, with light shear and warm sea-surface temperatures across the central Gulf of Mexico supporting additional strengthening tonight and Tuesday.

The initial motion estimate is 310/12, and Solene should continue on a similar northwestward heading through Tuesday as it moves around the western periphery of a mid-level ridge centered over the southeastern United States. A slower, more northward turn is expected by Tuesday night as the ridge weakens, bringing the system toward the northern Gulf coast near landfall.

Key messages:

1. Life-threatening storm surge is possible along portions of the Louisiana and Mississippi coast where a Storm Surge Warning is in effect.

2. Hurricane-force winds are expected within the warning area beginning late Tuesday, with tropical-storm-force winds arriving well in advance of the core.

3. Heavy rainfall may produce flash and urban flooding across southeast Louisiana into Wednesday.

Forecaster Demo/Solene (SIMULATED STORM — DEMO DATA)
